questions.question: What does crossing_cycle(records, threshold=1.5) return?
options: The first cycle whose capability-minus-alignment gap reaches 1.5, or -1 if none does
The cycle with the highest alignment value
The average cycle count across scenarios
The last cycle regardless of the gap
questions.explanation: The function scans the signed C-A gap in order and returns the first cycle with gap >= threshold; it uses -1 when no crossing occurs.

questions.question: How does run update capability C and alignment A at each cycle?
options: It adds the rates once and never uses noise
It multiplies each value by a noisy rate, clamping each rate to at least .9
It sets both values to their average
It subtracts alignment from capability before every update
questions.explanation: Each cycle samples a Gaussian perturbation around r_c or r_a, applies max(.9, rate), and multiplies the current C or A by that factor.

questions.question: What does Scenario B (r_c=1.10, r_a=1.10) demonstrate most directly?
options: Capability always outruns alignment
Alignment is held at exactly zero
Equal mean growth rates do not create a systematic capability lead, though noise can move the gap
The threshold can never be evaluated
questions.explanation: With equal expected rates, compounding does not favor one series on average; the sampled noise still permits temporary positive or negative gaps.

questions.question: When does print_trajectory label a row PAUSE?
options: Whenever cycle is odd
Whenever alignment is larger than capability
Only at cycle zero
When the recorded gap capability - alignment is at least 1.5
questions.explanation: The display uses the same signed C-A gap threshold as crossing_cycle and marks that trajectory point for a pause.

questions.question: Why does a higher mean alignment rate in Scenario C not prove that a run is safe?
options: Capability and alignment are compounded through noisy samples, so a particular capability trajectory can still create a large gap
The code never updates alignment
Scenario C has no threshold
The rates are converted to additive scores
questions.explanation: Scenario C has r_a=1.13 versus r_c=1.10, but stochastic compounding and the path of each run still determine whether the pause gap is reached.

questions.question: Which quantity is compared with the threshold 1.5?
options: The ratio C/A
The signed capability-minus-alignment gap C-A
The number of Monte Carlo trials
The sum of the two rates
questions.explanation: Both crossing_cycle and the display compare the signed C-A gap, not a ratio or a rate sum.
